source: Karpathy AutoResearch
summary: AutoResearch runs 100+ ML experiments overnight in a self-improving loop, keeping only changes that beat the current best result; picked up 21k stars in March 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — focused on ML experiment loops rather than software agent orchestration; no direct mapping to the state-machine / CLI subprocess model.

source: Karpathy Agentic Engineering (Sequoia Ascent 2026)
summary: Karpathy coins 'agentic engineering' to describe disciplined AI-assisted development — conceptual ownership, reviewing diffs for architecture, building eval loops, preserving security boundaries.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — philosophical framing for engineering practice; no concrete technical pattern to implement.

source: SICA Self-Improving Coding Agent (Univ. Bristol)
summary: SICA unifies meta-agent and target-agent into one system that edits its own prompts and tools based on execution feedback; achieved 53% SWE-bench by mid-2025.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — the concept maps to self-improving prompt templates in AgentForge's promptRenderer, but adapting it to CLI subprocess agents (not API-based) requires new infrastructure (prompt versioning, A/B testing, eval harness).

source: Escher-Loop: Mutual Evolution by Closed-Loop Self-Referential Optimization
summary: Maintains two co-evolving populations — task agents and optimizer agents — using relative win-loss signals for dynamic benchmarking; ICML 2026 AI4Math Workshop poster.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — fascinating mutual evolution concept but requires two agent populations and a fitness evaluation harness; architecture mismatch with AgentForge's single-agent-per-stage model.

source: DemoEvolve: Overcoming Sparse Feedback in Agentic Harness Evolution
summary: Addresses sparse reward in agentic harness evolution by seeding the improvement loop with human demonstrations to bootstrap signal.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — requires human-provided demonstrations to function; AgentForge has no mechanism to collect or store demonstration data.

source: The Kitchen Loop: User-Spec-Driven Development for a Self-Evolving Codebase
summary: Agents continuously evolve a codebase by iterating against user specifications; the codebase itself becomes the agent's output artifact.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — product-level vision rather than an orchestration pattern; AgentForge already has a similar loop (Linear issue → implementation → review) but without the continuous codebase-as-artifact model.

source: PASTE: Act While Thinking — Pattern-Aware Speculative Tool Execution (SJTU + Microsoft Research)
summary: Predicts and pre-executes future tool calls while the LLM is still generating, based on recurring agent tool-call patterns; 48.5% average latency reduction, 1.8x throughput improvement.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low-Medium — designed for API-based agents with visible tool invocations; AgentForge's tools execute inside opaque CLI subprocesses, making pre-execution speculation at the orchestrator layer impractical without major subprocess transparency changes.

source: B-PASTE: Beam-Aware Pattern-Guided Speculative Execution
summary: Extends PASTE with beam-aware scheduling for resource-constrained environments; further reduces tail latency under limited GPU capacity.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — same subprocess-transparency limitation as PASTE; also targets GPU-serving scenarios not relevant to CLI subprocesses.

source: Speculative Interaction Agents: Real-Time Agents with Async I/O and Speculative Tool Calling
summary: Builds real-time interactive agents using asynchronous I/O and speculative tool pre-execution to eliminate perceived latency in user-facing systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — targets interactive real-time UX scenarios; AgentForge runs long-horizon async batch jobs where user-perceived latency per tool call is not a design constraint.

source: AgenticCache: Cache-Driven Asynchronous Planning for Embodied AI Agents
summary: Uses KV-cache-driven asynchronous planning to reduce perception-action latency in embodied agents operating in physical environments.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — embodied AI / robotics focus; no mapping to software orchestration pipeline.

source: Zylos AI: Graceful Degradation Patterns in AI Agent Systems
summary: Documents a 7-layer degradation strategy (error classification → retries → circuit breakers → bulkheads → fallback models → queue buffering → human escalation) with production failure rate data showing 41-86.7% unmitigated failure rates in multi-agent systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps directly to AgentForge's missing graceful degradation in ProcessRunner; AIBlocked with no retry is the exact gap addressed.

source: Mindra: Fault-Tolerant AI Agents — Failure Handling, Retry, Fallback
summary: Engineering guide covering retry with exponential backoff, circuit breakers, compensating actions, and human escalation for production multi-agent systems; cites 41%+ failure rates without deliberate resilience design.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — directly informs the circuit-breaker retry implementation in AgentForge's ProcessRunner (co-inspiration for HID-141).

source: ZEBRA: Zero-shot Budgeted Resource Allocation for LLM Orchestration (ETH Zürich / Stanford)
summary: Frames multi-phase budget allocation as a continuous knapsack problem with per-phase utility curves; recovers 94.4% of unconstrained quality at 50% of spend; 14.3pp advantage over LLM-direct allocation on HotpotQA.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — maps directly to AgentForge's sequential stage machine (plan, planReview, implement, codeReview, addressing); zero-shot profile fits AgentForge's current lack of historical token usage data.

source: BATS: Budget-Aware Tool-Use Enables Effective Agent Scaling (UC Santa Barbara / Google)
summary: Lightweight Budget Tracker plug-in that provides agents continuous budget awareness, adjusting stepwise planning and verification strategies based on remaining resources; outperforms unconstrained agents on SWE-bench-style web tasks.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — Budget Tracker pattern informs the per-stage maxTokens injection in AgentForge's prompt envelope; complementary to ZEBRA for implementation details (co-inspiration for HID-143).

source: Cost-Aware Speculative Execution for LLM-Agent Workflows: Five-Dimension Method
summary: Integrated five-dimension framework for cost-aware speculative execution in LLM pipelines; covers computation, memory, latency, quality, and financial cost trade-offs.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — broader survey of the cost-optimization space; ZEBRA and BATS cover the most directly applicable patterns for AgentForge's sequential pipeline.

source: On Time, Within Budget: Constraint-Driven Online Resource Allocation for Agentic Workflows
summary: Online constraint satisfaction approach for allocating time and budget resources across agentic workflow phases under dynamic arrival rates.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — online allocation is appealing but AgentForge runs sequential (not concurrent) pipelines, so the constraint-satisfaction complexity is not yet warranted.

source: Token Budgets: Empirical Catalog of 63 LLM-Agent Budget-Overrun Incidents
summary: Empirical catalog of 63 confirmed budget-overrun incidents from 21 orchestration frameworks (2023-2026), organized into an eight-cluster failure taxonomy with Rust mitigation case study.
relevanceToAgentForge: Medium — motivational data for adding budget controls; the failure taxonomy is useful for designing the BudgetController edge-case tests in HID-143.

source: OpenTelemetry GenAI Semantic Conventions
summary: Finalized semantic conventions for LLM and agent observability including gen_ai.system, gen_ai.operation.name, gen_ai.usage.input_tokens/output_tokens span attributes; adopted by AWS, Braintrust, Galileo in 2026.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — provides the standard span schema for instrumenting AgentForge's per-stage CLI subprocess invocations without inventing a proprietary telemetry format.

source: AWS AgentCore Observability (AgentOps on Amazon Bedrock)
summary: AWS AgentCore uses OTEL GenAI conventions to track decision traces, tool invocation patterns, latency, errors, memory usage, and cost per agent interaction in production at scale.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — production validation that OTEL GenAI spans are sufficient for full agent observability; confirms the approach in HID-142 is production-grade (co-inspiration).

source: Augment Code: AI Agent Monitoring Guide 2026
summary: Practical 2026 guide covering agent telemetry via OpenTelemetry trace-span hierarchy, per-stage cost attribution, and the metric targets (>85% goal achievement rate, <5% error rate, <5000 tokens/task) for production agent systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: High — defines the metric targets for AgentForge's getRunTelemetrySummary helper in HID-142; validates the OTEL-first approach for CLI-subprocess monitoring.

source: OpenEvolve: Evolutionary Coding Agent
summary: Open-source evolutionary coding agent that applies genetic-algorithm-style mutation and selection to code; population-based approach to discovering better implementations.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — evolutionary/population-based approach requires a fitness evaluation harness and parallel execution infrastructure that AgentForge does not have; sequential single-agent model is incompatible.

source: VoltAgent Awesome AI Agent Papers 2026
summary: Curated collection of AI agent research papers released in 2026, covering engineering, memory, evaluation, workflows, and autonomous systems.
relevanceToAgentForge: Low — resource aggregator, not a specific innovation; useful as a discovery index for future runs.
